title: 저희 왜 한우 사주세요?  (Why Are You Buying Us Korean Beef?)

segments.t: At a barbecue restaurant that night, Ra Joon-mo treats his writers to pricey Korean beef — which instantly tips off Son Ji-yeon that something is wrong with the show. Listen for the terms for 'premium Korean beef' and 'cast replacement'.
전화해봤는데 지금 마포대교를 건너고 계신대요.
맨날 거길 건너고 있어!
근데 저희 왜 한우 사주세요? 이상한데.
우리 없어져요?
폐지는 아니고 멤버 교체하래.
일 좀 두 번 시키지 마요, 피곤해 죽겠는데.
우리는 가는 거 맞아요?
누가 너네 잘린대? 내가 그런 사람이야?
Let's unpack the eight lines of this smoky barbecue-table confrontation.
전화해봤는데 지금 마포대교를 건너고 계신대요.

It literally means this. 'I called her and she says she's crossing Mapo Bridge right now.' Hours after the afternoon meeting, the head writer is still using the exact same bridge excuse! The opening word phrase means 'I tried calling her, and...' It is a handy word.
맨날 거길 건너고 있어!

It literally means this. 'She's crossing that bridge every single day!' Fed up, Joon-mo pairs the word for 'every day, always' with the contracted form of 'that place', joking next that she must live on the bridge It comes from this.
근데 저희 왜 한우 사주세요? 이상한데.

It literally means this. 'Wait, why are you buying us Korean beef? That's suspicious.' Much more expensive than pork belly, prized domestic Korean beef is reserved for big celebrations — or guilty bad news! The closing remark comes from the word meaning 'strange' or 'fishy' Notice the word for.
우리 없어져요?
It literally means this. 'Are we getting cancelled?' Sharp as a tack, Ji-yeon jumps straight to asking literally 'are we disappearing?'. In TV talk, 'we' means the show itself It is a handy word.
폐지는 아니고 멤버 교체하래.

It literally means this. 'It's not a cancellation, they told us to replace the cast.' Forced to come clean, Joon-mo contrasts 'cancellation' with 'cast replacement'. The word ending passes along orders from upstairs: 'they told me to swap them' This short for that.
일 좀 두 번 시키지 마요, 피곤해 죽겠는데.

It literally means this. 'Please don't make us do the work twice, I'm dead tired.' Because she already researched Miss A, Ji-yeon groans 'don't make me do it twice'. Remember 'cold to death' earlier? Here she uses the same pattern for 'tired to death!' It comes from this.
우리는 가는 거 맞아요?

It literally means this. 'Is it certain that we writers are staying on?' Unlike salaried staff producers, freelance writers can lose their income overnight. Here the middle phrase means 'continuing forward together', checked with the tag question 'is that right?' Swap in this word.
누가 너네 잘린대? 내가 그런 사람이야?

It literally means this. 'Who says you're getting cut? Am I that kind of person?' The word for getting cut literally means 'get snipped off', Korean's everyday slang for getting fired. Loyal to his crew, Joon-mo bristles with 'do you take me for that sort of guy?' Swap in this word. Now let's listen to the whole Korean beef dinner scene again.
전화해봤는데 지금 마포대교를 건너고 계신대요.
맨날 거길 건너고 있어!
근데 저희 왜 한우 사주세요? 이상한데.
우리 없어져요?
폐지는 아니고 멤버 교체하래.
일 좀 두 번 시키지 마요, 피곤해 죽겠는데.
우리는 가는 거 맞아요?
누가 너네 잘린대? 내가 그런 사람이야?
You learned the words for prized Korean beef, when something feels fishy, being tired, and getting cut. One cosy family finale to go!
안녕히 가세요!
